summary_en: This work explains and analyzes spread-spectrum color Doppler ultrasound, in which plane waves are transmitted over repeated azimuth-angle sequences whose ordering is randomized between repetitions. The coding causes in-focus and off-focus echoes to have different slow-time modulation, enabling stationary clutter suppression with a notching comb filter without conventional compounding. The paper develops a simplified signal model, studies discrete-time comb-filter implementations, compares source-localization behavior with single-plane-wave Doppler imaging, and characterizes sensitivity to tissue motion. It is a direct acoustic-coded-imaging contribution, but should remain in the candidate collection until peer-reviewed publication metadata becomes available.
